cr_data.provenance: Private collection, Amarillo, Texas, before 1959; Andrew Smith, Santa Fe, New Mexico, and Gerald Peters Gallery, Santa Fe, New Mexico, 1978 (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks. "Pat I wrote for entry cards for the Philadelphia Watercolor Club tonight & we're going & fill two out for you for the Hollyhocks [lost drawing] & Monotype [*Untitled (Portrait of Dorothy True)*]" (Anita Pollitzer to O'Keeffe, October 1915, *Lovingly Georgia* [1990], p. 44); "Your monotype is very strong & they gave it a good position. . . .It's the one of Dorothy with very red hair" (Anita Pollitzer to O'Keeffe, November 1915, *Lovingly Georgia* [1990], p. 81). Dorothy True was a friend of O'Keeffe and Pollitzer. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.title: Untitled (Portrait of Dorothy True)

description: A woman, seen in profile, looks downward with a neutral expression. Her hair is a bright orangish-yellow, which contrasts with her dark brown coat. The background is gray and dotted with round, white shapes that resemble snowflakes. The work is simple and composed of large shapes with little detail.
title: Untitled (Portrait of Dorothy True)
